az_upper_beach.blurb: Upper Beach is a small south-facing crag in the Beach Areas of West Twin Butte, on the edge of Sedona at roughly 5,100 feet. Twelve climbs mix trad and sport, mostly 5.10 and 5.11 with a single 5.9 and one 5.12, so it suits leaders already comfortable in the low double digits. Because the wall looks straight south it soaks up sun for much of the day, which makes it a pleasant choice in the colder months, and the outlook over the valley is wide. The stone is cleaner than at many Sedona walls, with ripples, pockets and sharp cracks, though the soft local rock stays fragile and the way up is a steep, loose gully scramble.
az_upper_beach.approach: Reach the ledge by scrambling up a steep, loose gully; take care with rock underfoot. Most of the routes are toward the right-hand side of the wall.

az_sven_tower_1.blurb: Sven Tower 1 is the farthest of the three Sven Towers, a granite crag in the McDowell Mountains near Scottsdale, reached on foot from the Tom's Thumb trailhead area. About a dozen routes are listed, mostly trad with a few sport lines and some top-rope options, running from easy fifth-class terrain up to 5.10, with a handful of 5.7 and 5.8 climbs in the middle. That spread makes it a good fit for moderate leaders and newer climbers building mileage. Expect a moderate hike with some scrambling and light brush, following cairns; sorting out the right trail the first time can take a little patience.

az_opera_house_hot_spot.blurb: Opera House, Hot Spot is a steep crack-climbing zone inside Lower Sullivan Canyon, a basalt gorge a few miles north of Chino Valley in the Prescott area. All twelve routes are trad and nearly all sit at 5.10, with a lone 5.9 and two 5.11s, so it rewards climbers who are at ease on sustained cracks. At least one line is a wide off-width, and a rack with doubles plus a big cam or two is the usual plan. The wall faces southwest and runs very warm in sun, so it is a place for cooler days. The heavily pocketed stone gives plenty of face holds between the cracks.

az_snake_flake_the.blurb: The Snake Flake is a basalt wall on the west side of Golden Valley in the Black Mountains outside Kingman. Of its twelve routes, eleven are sport and one is trad, spread from 5.7 up to 5.12 with a friendly cluster of 5.7 and 5.8 lines, so newer leaders have real options alongside a few 5.10 and 5.11 tests. The wall faces east, so mornings are sunny and the afternoon brings shade. Routes are short to moderate in length, with pockets and edges on solid volcanic stone. Neighbouring walls such as the Prow and Dall Wall are close by, so it combines easily with a longer day.

az_ghost_town.blurb: Ghost Town is a small, scrappy crag tucked into the folds of the San Francisco Peaks north of Flagstaff, up in the burned forest at roughly 9,000 feet. Twelve climbs, mostly trad with two sport lines, run from 5.9 to 5.11 and cluster at 5.10, with crisp cracks but loose rock in places. It faces southwest and catches plenty of sun, and the stone dries quickly after rain. A long bike-and-hike approach keeps the crowds away, and the views and summer wildflowers are the real draw. Lines are short, so it suits a quiet outing rather than a big-mileage day.

az_upper_looner_land.blurb: Upper Looner Land is a small cluster of towers in the Mine Area of Queen Creek Canyon near Superior, a little west of Lower Looner Land where two big washes meet. Of the twelve routes, eleven are sport and one is trad. Grades are friendly: plenty of 5.7 and 5.8, a few 5.9 and 5.10 lines, and just a couple of harder routes up to 5.12. Stone in this part of the canyon varies from pocketed to edgy, and the moderate offerings make the Mine Area a popular choice. The walk in follows the wash west from the lot, or continues about five minutes past Lower Looner Land.
